evals.name: torn-paper-edge-generator
evals.prompt: /prototype:build-generator The cover of our annual report page needs a torn paper edge along the bottom of the hero photo. I have asked for it twice and each time it is closer but not quite: the tears look too regular and the fibers are missing. The site is a Vite + React app.
evals.expected_output: A round of 'closer, but not quite' has already happened, so the skill says the loop is the evidence and stops prompting for the edge directly. Before any code it pitches the tool in four parts: the gap (the tear's irregularity is a judgment call only the user's eye can make), the tool (a dial-in generator that rebuilds the tearing process, rendered at the size it ships), the controls (such as tear depth, jaggedness, fiber density, seed) and the export (a JSON config, plus the path or SVG data the cover imports). The tool lives on an isolated, disposable route inside the app; every control has tested bounds, everything re-renders live, clicking draws a new seed, and save writes the full config to a JSON file in the project and shows the written path. The handoff is two lines (the URL and the verbs) and then it stops; it does not wire anything into the real cover before the user picks a keeper.
expectations: The response names the earlier 'closer, but not quite' rounds as the reason to build a tool instead of prompting for the edge again
Before writing any tool code, the response pitches the gap, the tool, the controls and the export
The generator rebuilds the tearing process with every taste value (such as jaggedness or depth) on a live control with stated bounds, rather than tracing one fixed edge
Save writes the full configuration to a JSON file in the project and shows the written path
The handoff gives the route URL and what to do with it, then stops without further suggestions
The response does not wire the generated edge into the real cover before the user picks a keeper

evals.name: save-output-harvests-and-deletes
evals.expected_output: The first word is the save-output action, so the skill harvests: it reads the saved config at the given path (and the export, if separate) rather than copying values off the panel, wires the export and the cleaned-up render logic into the real artifact, records the answer as the discipline's When done section says, then deletes the tool's route, controls and save endpoint while the saved config and export stay.
expectations: The response reads the values from lab/torn-edge/saved/keeper.json, not from the panel or a screenshot
The real artifact imports the saved config or a static export made from it
The tool's route, controls and save endpoint are deleted
The saved config file is kept, not deleted with the tool

evals.name: fully-determined-builds-directly
evals.prompt: /prototype:build-generator a 1px solid #e5e7eb divider line under the page header
evals.expected_output: The result is fully determined, with no judgment call left, so the skill does not build a generator: it says a tool would be overhead here and builds the divider directly.
expectations: The response says a generator is not worth building because nothing is left for the user's eye to decide
No lab route, control panel or save endpoint is created
The divider is built directly with the stated 1px solid #e5e7eb values
